text: Welcome

This guide teaches you the Distribution Management System (DMS) project from zero. You only need basic C: printf, scanf, for and while loops, simple arrays, and if/else. Everything else is explained here as we go.
Think of DMS as a practice warehouse game in your terminal. Company holds big stock, dealers buy from company, shops (retailers) buy from dealers. You log in, view tables, and place orders.
What you will learn
What the project does in real life (supply chain).
How to compile and run the program on your computer.
What every file does and how they connect.
New ideas: functions, multiple files, strings, 2D arrays, extern.
How ordering works step by step, with real numbers.
1. The Big Picture
1.1 Real-world story

A rice company keeps 100 bags in a central warehouse. A dealer in Dhaka orders 20 bags. A shop in Mirpur orders 5 bags from that dealer. Customers buy from the shop. DMS simulates this chain on your screen.

2. Build and Run (Start Here)
2.1 Open terminal in project folder
cd /path/to/DMS
2.2 Compile all C files together
C projects often split code into many .c files. GCC compiles each file and links them into one program called dms.
gcc main.c data.c display.c company.c dealer.c retailer.c -o dms
2.3 Run the program
./dms
2.4 Quick test session
Main menu: choose 2 (Dealer Login).
Enter Dealer ID: 1 (Dhaka Dealer).
Password: 1122.
Choose 3 (Order From Company), Product ID 1, Quantity 10.
Choose 0 to logout, then 0 again to exit.
If gcc is missing on Mac: run xcode-select --install

text: 3.1 How files talk to each other
A header file (.h) lists what exists (function names, variables). A source file (.c) contains the real code. #include "data.h" at the top of a file means: use the shared data declared in data.h.

#include "data.h"   /* I need product lists and stock arrays */
#include "display.h" /* I need print_menu_item, print_error, etc. */
4. C Basics You Already Know
Before new ideas, here is how familiar syntax appears in DMS.
4.1 printf — show text

printf("Enter your choice: ");  /* no newline at end */
printf("Welcome, %s\n", dealer_name[dealer_index]);  /* %s = string */
4.2 scanf — read input

scanf("%d", &choice);     /* read integer into choice */
scanf("%s", password);    /* read word into char array */
4.3 for loop — walk through a list
4.4 do-while — menu until user exits
5. New Ideas in This Project
5.1 Functions
A function is a named block of code you can call. void means it returns nothing. int means it returns a number (like 1 for true, 0 for false).
5.2 char arrays = strings
In C there is no separate string type. Text lives in char name[50] — up to 49 letters plus end marker. Use strcpy to copy text and strcmp to compare.
5.3 2D arrays — stock grid
dealer_stock[dealer][product] is a table: row = which dealer, column = which product. Example: dealer_stock[0][0] = Dhaka Dealer's Rice count.
5.4 extern — one copy of data for all files
Arrays are defined once in data.c. data.h says extern so company.c, dealer.c, and retailer.c all use the same stock numbers. When a dealer orders, company stock changes everywhere immediately.
5.5 break and return
break — stop a for loop early when you found the right ID.
return — leave a function immediately (used after errors so bad orders don't run).

text: 7. main.c — Program Boss
Every C program starts at main(). DMS loads data, then loops on the main menu until you choose Exit (0).
8. display.c — Screens and Tables
All pretty printing lives here. Other files call these helpers so menus look the same everywhere.
print_menu_header / print_menu_item — boxed menus.
print_table_product_row — one line of a stock table.
verify_password() — compares input to 1122.
print_error / print_success — user feedback.
print_order_summary — after a successful order.
9. company.c — Company Panel
Company logs in with password only. It views data — no ordering in this version.

Show dealer table.

Password 1122, then dealer menu opens.
10.2 The found pattern (used everywhere)
10.3 Ordering from company
Three checks before stock moves: product exists, quantity > 0, company has enough stock. Then two lines of math:

company_stock[product_index] -= quantity;
dealer_stock[dealer_index][product_index] += quantity;
Example: Company Rice 100 → 90, Dhaka Dealer Rice 20 → 30 after ordering 10 units.
11. retailer.c — Shop Panel
Same ideas as dealer, but retailers order from their linked dealer (retailer_dealer[]). Stock moves from dealer_stock down to retailer_stock.

dealer_stock[dealer_index][product_index] -= quantity;
retailer_stock[retailer_index][product_index] += quantity;

text: 14. Practice Exercises
Easy
Change the password in display.c and test login.
Add a 4th product in init_data() (e.g. Salt).
Medium
Add menu option: dealer sees total units across all products.
Print which dealer a retailer is linked to on login.
Hard
Save stock to a file on exit and load on start (needs file I/O).
Reject orders that would leave seller with zero stock of everything.
